evidence: Kew/POWO accepts Pluchea camphorata and lists Texas within its native range.
Hays County — Purola Preserve lists P. camphorata among naturally occurring plants, separate from its introduced-species list.
Travis County — the University of Texas Plant Resources Center Travis County Asteraceae herbarium index includes a P. camphorata specimen.

Regional Texas flora material places the species in eastern and central Texas westward to the Edwards Plateau, but B016 did not recover a third exact target county from an authoritative occurrence source.
target_zone_range.blocking_issue: Two project counties are firm. Broad 'central Texas to Edwards Plateau' distribution is not converted into a third county without an exact county record.
target_zone_range.guardrail: Common-name confusion is high: Heterotheca subaxillaris is also called camphorweed and has yellow radiate heads. Pluchea camphorata has pink-purple discoid heads and should not be identified from odor alone.

morphology.look_here_first: Start with the leaf arrangement and head type: alternate, resinous/gland-dotted, usually petiolate leaves below a rounded cluster of many tiny pink-purple heads with no ray florets.
diagnostic_traits: annual to short-lived perennial herb of moist to wet nonsaline soils
leaves alternate, simple, elliptic to oblong/lanceolate, usually visibly petiolate to subsessile
leaf margins usually serrate; surfaces resinous/gland-dotted
crushed foliage may have a camphor-like odor, useful only as a secondary cue
inflorescence a rounded or corymbiform/paniculiform mass of numerous small heads
heads discoid with pink to purple florets and no ray florets
phyllaries cream to purplish, largely granular-glandular to nearly glabrous
fruit a cypsela with a capillary pappus

confusers.separator: P. odorata usually has less distinctly petiolate leaves and more puberulent involucral parts; P. camphorata has more obvious petioles and inner phyllaries that are thin and comparatively glabrous.
Both may be called camphorweed, but Heterotheca has conspicuous yellow ray florets; Pluchea camphorata has only small pink-purple disk florets.
Blue mistflower has opposite triangular 3-veined leaves and blue-violet heads; Pluchea has alternate resinous leaves and pink-purple heads.

installation_guardrail: Do not install as a project-native until three target-zone counties are documented or Calvin explicitly approves a documented exception.
